title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page is the blank back of a June 1978 Montpellier exam sheet (C4, option of M. Petrich, on conjugacy classes of A5 and the icosahedron). The exam text has nothing to do with the notes. The notes belong to Grothendieck's 'Teichmüller groupoid' material. The next page computes H^1(S_5, M_{0,5}; G_m), H^0(M_{0,K}, G_m) and H^2(T_{0,5}^+, Z). So the aim is the S_n-equivariant Picard group of the open moduli space M_{0,I} (n = |I| marked points on P^1). Equivalently, it is the Picard group of the stack M_{0,n}/S_n of n unordered points. In particular he wants explicit torsion line bundles on it. Reconstruction:
(1) Let L_i be the cotangent line at the i-th marked point (the psi line bundle on the open part). For a 3-element subset A of I (A ∈ P_3(I)) with i ∈ A, and an ordering ω of the two other points b, c, there is a unique coordinate z with z(i)=0, z(b)=1, z(c)=∞. Its differential dz at i gives a trivialization φ_{i,A,ω}: L_i → O.
(2) Exchanging b and c replaces z by z/(z-1), whose derivative at 0 is -1. So φ changes to -φ (the note 'ξ ∈ L_i, -ξ'). Hence the square is independent of ω and gives a canonical trivialization ψ_{i,A}: L_i^2 ≅ O, i.e. a canonical nowhere-vanishing section ξ*_{i,A} ∈ Γ(L_i^2).
(3) Taking the product over i ∈ A with a cyclic orientation ε of A gives ξ_A ∈ Γ(L_A^{(*)}), where L_A = ⊗_{i∈A} L_i. Under a transposition of A each of the three factors flips sign, so ξ_A changes sign: it is a section of L_A twisted by the orientation character (the 'L_ε' and 'L_A^{2~}' notations).
(4) The product ξ = ∏_A ξ_A over all A ∈ P_3(I) is a section of ⊗_A L_A = L^{⊗ν}. Here L = ⊗_{i∈I} L_i and ν = #{A ∋ i} = C(n-1,2) = (n-1)(n-2)/2. ξ is S_I-invariant up to a sign character, so its square is invariant. This yields an S_I-equivariant trivialization of L^{⊗2ν}, i.e. a torsion class in Pic(M_{0,n}/S_n).
(5) Examples: n=4, ν=3, giving L^{⊗6} ≅ 1. For n=5, ν=6, he writes L^{⊗6} ≅ 1 again.
(6) Last line: a comparison of L_i with L ⊗ L_{I∖{i}}^{-1}, i.e. with a pullback of O(±1) along the forgetful map p_i: M_{0,I} → M_{0,I∖{i}} (identified with a curve Σ). This is presumably meant to relate the bundles for n and n-1 inductively.
On the scheme M_{0,I} itself Pic = 0 (it is an open subset of affine space), as the next page notes: H^1(M_{0,5}; G_m) = 0. So all the content is in the equivariance, to be computed via H^1(S_n, H^0(M_{0,n}, G_m)), with H^0 = G_m × (cross-ratio lattice).
errors: The right-hand formula is transcribed as ν=(n-1)(n-1)/2; it must be (n-1)(n-2)/2, the number of 3-subsets containing a fixed i. That value agrees with ν=3 for n=4 and ν=6 for n=5.

For n=5 the construction as described gives a canonical trivialization of L^{⊗2ν}=L^{⊗12} (up to sign characters), not obviously L^{⊗6}. The written 'L^{⊗6} ≅ 1' for n=5 is either a slip copied from n=4 or relies on an extra argument not on the page.
The arrow M_{0,I} → M_{0,A} with A a 3-subset is degenerate, since M_{0,A} is a point. It probably means a 4-element set, or just signals restriction of structure to the points of A.

The pieces individually trivialize L_i^2 for each A, but non-canonically across different A. The ratios ψ_{i,A}/ψ_{i,A'} are units on M_{0,I} (cross-ratio type), and only products over all A are S_n-equivariant. This is not spelled out on the page.

ideas.what: Canonical trivialization, up to sign, of the cotangent line at marked point i using a 3-subset A ∋ i (normalized coordinate 0,1,∞). The sign ambiguity disappears in the square.
ideas.modern_name: trivialization of psi line bundles on the open M_{0,n} via cross-ratio coordinates

ideas.what: Product over all 3-subsets gives an S_n-equivariant (up to sign character) trivialization of L^{⊗2ν}, L = ⊗ψ_i, ν = C(n-1,2). Torsion line bundles on the stack M_{0,n}/S_n (e.g. order dividing 6 for n=4).
ideas.modern_name: torsion in the Picard group of the stack of n unordered points on P^1 / M_{0,n}/S_n
ideas.usually_credited_to: Arsie–Vistoli (2004) and related work on Picard groups of stacks of hyperelliptic curves and of unordered points; Mumford (Pic M_{1,1}=Z/12, 1965)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses Teichmüller groupoids of M_{0,n} with S_n action, but not this computation as far as known

ideas.what: Computing the equivariant Picard group via H^1(S_n, H^0(M_{0,n},G_m)), using the explicit unit group (constants plus cross-ratio lattice). Set up on the next page.
ideas.modern_name: equivariant Picard group via the Hochschild–Serre / Leray spectral sequence for a group quotient

missed.claim: Explicit S_n-equivariant torsion line bundles on M_{0,n} are built from psi-classes. A general formula ν=(n-1)(n-2)/2 gives an exponent 2ν, but the optimal order is left unsettled: n=5 is given as 6 rather than 12. The construction suggests the order of the class of ⊗ψ_i in Pic(M_{0,n}/S_n) and its relation to the sign character.
missed.quote: ν = (n-1)(n-2)/2 ... Ex n=4, ν=3 on trouve L^{⊗6} ≃ 1 ; Ex n=5, ν=6, on trouve L^{⊗6} ≃ 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Pic of the stack of unordered points on P^1 is known (Arsie–Vistoli and successors), so this is mostly an early, explicit, cross-ratio-based approach. It could give canonical explicit generators, but is unlikely to be new as a result.

missed.claim: The n=4 case (order 6 class built from psi-lines on M_{0,4}/S_4) sits next to the well-known Pic(M_{1,1})=Z/12 via the Legendre/2-torsion picture. The note implicitly links psi-class torsion in genus 0 with Hodge-bundle torsion in genus 1, in the Teichmüller tower context.
missed.quote: Ex n=4, ν=3 on trouve L^{⊗6} ≃ 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. This relationship is understood via hyperelliptic/2-torsion covers, so it is only of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a genuine but small computation: canonical psi-line trivializations and S_n-equivariant torsion in Pic of M_{0,n}/S_n, preparing the Teichmüller-groupoid cohomology on the next page. The ingredients are standard, and Picard groups of these quotient stacks were later computed in the literature. It is of historical interest as an early (≥1978) Grothendieck computation, not a missing result.
transcription_corrections: The struck-through prefactor near ν=(n-1)(n-2)/2 at top right is an overwritten '*' and denominator '2'.
'L_i —φ_{i,A,ω}→ O' is a map (trivialization) of L_i to O; 'L_i^2 ≃_{ψ_{i,A}} O' is an isomorphism; a crossed-out line 'L_i ≃ O' is struck through by Grothendieck himself.
'𝓛_ε' near 'A' is likely an orientation/sign-character twist (L_A twisted by ε), consistent with 'ξ ∈ L_A^{2~}'.
Final line: 'p_i : M_{0,I} → M_{0,I∖{i}} ≃ Σ'. The term p_i^*(O(1)) has an uncertain sign (could be O(-1)).
Left-margin sketches: three dots and a line through three dots, probably pictures of marked points on a curve. The '72' at bottom left is the archive page number.
